The key-term table suggests bare 'rintis'. Please confirm 'program rintis', or change it everywhere.

pages.organisations.intro.note: Translator: 'underserved youth' is translated as 'belia yang kurang mendapat perkhidmatan'. 'Kurang terbela' is a common Malaysian alternative. Please choose one. pages.organisations.intro.back: Thinkerwell is a student-led platform and strives to widen access to free digital social studies learning for underserved youth across Southeast Asia. We are preparing pilot programmes of our course together with learning organisations. This page explains what is involved in the pilot programme.
pages.organisations.intro.source: Thinkerwell is a student-led platform working to expand access to free digital social studies learning for underserved youth across Southeast Asia. We are preparing a pilot of our course with learning organisations. This page explains what a pilot involves.

pages.organisations.honesty.note: Translator: 'nonprofit' is translated as 'pertubuhan bukan berasaskan keuntungan'. Please confirm this is the usual Malaysian wording. Back-translation check: Please confirm that 'pertubuhan bukan berasaskan keuntungan' is the usual Malaysian term for a nonprofit (alternative: 'pertubuhan bukan untung').
pages.organisations.honesty.back: Thinkerwell is a student-led platform. It is not a registered charity or non-profit organisation.
pages.organisations.honesty.source: Thinkerwell is a student-led platform. It is not a registered charity or nonprofit.

pages.organisations.whatBody.note: Back-translation check: Changed 'berjalan' (a calque of 'runs') to 'berfungsi' and lower-cased the language names. Check that the lower-case step names (baca, tulis, cakap, tonton, refleksi) are fine in running text.
pages.organisations.whatBody.back: One course, Exploring Our World: {lessons} lessons about history, geography, culture and civic life, for learners aged about 10 to 17. Each lesson has five steps: read, write, speak, watch and reflect. The course runs in a web browser on shared laptops and tablets, in English, Indonesian or Malay. Lessons can be used offline after the first visit, but the videos, which are not compulsory, need the internet.
pages.organisations.whatBody.source: One course, Exploring Our World: {lessons} lessons about history, geography, culture and civic life, for learners aged about 10 to 17. Each lesson has five steps: read, write, speak, watch and reflect. It runs in a web browser on shared laptops and tablets, in English, Bahasa Indonesia or Bahasa Melayu. Lessons work offline after the first visit; the optional videos need the internet.

pages.organisations.get1.back: The whole course, free. No accounts, no ads and nothing locked.
pages.organisations.get1.source: The whole course, free. No accounts, no ads, and nothing locked.

pages.organisations.get2.back: A teacher's guide for every lesson, answer keys for the section checks, and every lesson ready to print.
pages.organisations.get2.source: A teacher guide for every lesson, answer keys for the section checks, and every lesson ready to print.

pages.organisations.get3.back: What you need to get started: an information sheet and consent form for families, code cards for learners and a checklist for each device.
pages.organisations.get3.source: What you need to start: an information sheet and a consent form for families, code cards for learners and a checklist for each device.

pages.organisations.get4.back: Answers to your questions by email, and changes to the course based on what you tell us.
pages.organisations.get4.source: Answers to your questions by email, and changes to the course based on what you tell us.

pages.organisations.ask1.back: One contact person at your organisation.
pages.organisations.ask1.source: One contact person at your organisation.

pages.organisations.ask2.back: Some laptops or tablets with a web browser. Learners can share devices.
pages.organisations.ask2.source: Some laptops or tablets with a web browser. Learners can share them.

pages.organisations.ask3.back: A few sessions a week for 4 to 6 weeks. One lesson takes about {min}–{max} minutes.
pages.organisations.ask3.source: A few sessions a week for 4 to 6 weeks. A lesson takes about {min}–{max} minutes.

pages.organisations.ask4.back: Honest feedback: what works, what doesn't, and what confuses learners.
pages.organisations.ask4.source: Honest feedback: what worked, what didn't, and what confused learners.

pages.organisations.privacy1.back: Pilot groups can use codes instead of names. Each learner gets a code card, such as HLP-01, and types that code as their name. Only you keep the list that matches codes to names.
pages.organisations.privacy1.source: Pilot groups can use codes instead of names. Each learner gets a code card, like HLP-01, and types the code as their name. Only you keep the list that matches codes to names.

pages.organisations.privacy2.back: No accounts, no email addresses and no ads. Learners' work stays on the device they use, and voice recordings never leave that device.
pages.organisations.privacy2.source: No accounts, no email addresses and no ads. Learners' work stays on the device they use, and voice recordings never leave it.

pages.organisations.privacy3.back: Parental consent. Before any learning data is shared with Thinkerwell, the parent or guardian signs a consent form, and the learner also says yes. This study will only use data linked to a code, never to a name: short questions and a few sentences in the first and last sessions, and, in every session, how the learner uses Thinkerwell: time, lessons and steps, answers, the help they used, videos and word counts, never what they write.
pages.organisations.privacy3.source: Parental consent. Before any learning data is shared with Thinkerwell, a parent or guardian signs a consent form, and the learner says yes too. The study would only use data linked to a code, never a name: short questions and a few sentences in the first and last sessions, and, in every session, how learners use Thinkerwell: time, lessons and steps, answers, the help they use, videos and word counts, never what they write.

pages.organisations.privacyNow.note: Translator: 'browser maker's service' is translated as 'perkhidmatan syarikat pembuat pelayar'. Check that families will understand it. Back-translation check: Check that families will understand 'perkhidmatan syarikat pembuat pelayar' (browser maker's service). It is accurate but wordy.
pages.organisations.privacyNow.back: For now, learners' work and progress are not sent to Thinkerwell. Online speech-to-text is turned off unless your staff turn it on; when it is on, what learners say is sent to the service of the company that makes the browser. We will tell you before anything else changes.
pages.organisations.privacyNow.source: Today, learners' work and progress are not sent to Thinkerwell. Online speech-to-text is off unless your staff turn it on; when it is on, what learners say goes to the browser maker's service. We will tell you before anything else changes.

pages.organisations.privacy4.back: Videos are not compulsory. Videos play from YouTube, only when the learner presses the play button, and every video has a written version.
pages.organisations.privacy4.source: Videos are optional. They play from YouTube, only when a learner taps play, and every video has a written version.

pages.organisations.startBody.back: Print what you need, and set up each device before the first session.
pages.organisations.startBody.source: Print what you need, and set up each device before the first session.

pages.organisations.contactBody.back: Email us to start a pilot programme or to ask a question. Tell us your organisation's name, your location, and roughly how many learners will take part.
pages.organisations.contactBody.source: Email us to start a pilot or to ask a question. Tell us your organisation's name, where you are, and about how many learners would take part.

pages.consentForm.intro.back: Print one form for each learner before the pilot programme starts: one page for the parent or guardian, and one page for the learner. Type your organisation's name to show it on the form, or leave it blank to write it by hand.
pages.consentForm.intro.source: Print one form for each learner before the pilot starts: a page for the parent or guardian, and a page for the learner. Type your organisation's name to put it on the form, or leave it empty to write it by hand.

pages.consentForm.orgHelper.back: It is only used on this form, and is not saved.
pages.consentForm.orgHelper.source: It is only used on this form, and is not saved.

pages.consentForm.staffTitle.back: For staff: this is a template
pages.consentForm.staffTitle.source: For staff: this is a template

pages.consentForm.staffBody.note: Back-translation check: 'Thinkerwell tidak pernah melihatnya' may carry a slight past-tense feel ('has never seen'). Check that it reads as a standing promise. The same wording is in consentForm.keep and pilotStudy.keepList.
pages.consentForm.staffBody.back: This is not legal advice. Before using it, check this form against your own organisation's rules and the data protection laws where you work, and change anything that does not fit. Signed forms contain names: keep them safely. Thinkerwell never sees them.
pages.consentForm.staffBody.source: It is not legal advice. Before you use it, check it against your organisation's own rules and the data protection law where you work, and change anything that doesn't fit. Signed forms have names on them: keep them safe. Thinkerwell never sees them.

pages.consentForm.staffUse.note: Translator: 'Tetapan' here refers to Thinkerwell's own Settings page, not the device menu. Back-translation check: 'turunkan tandatangan sebagai saksi' is quite formal. 'tandatangan sebagai saksi' may be plainer.
pages.consentForm.staffUse.back: Give the information sheet together with this form to each family. If the parent or guardian cannot read, read both aloud in their language, and put your signature as a witness on page 2. Learners aged 18 and over sign for themselves. This form does not cover online speech-to-text, so make sure that feature is turned off in Settings.
pages.consentForm.staffUse.source: Give each family the information sheet with the form. If a parent or guardian can't read, read both aloud in their language, and sign as a witness on page 2. Learners aged 18 or older sign for themselves. The form doesn't cover online speech-to-text, so keep it off in Settings.

pages.consentForm.formTitle.source: Taking part in the Thinkerwell pilot

pages.consentForm.formIntro.back: {organisation} is trying out Thinkerwell, a free online course about history, geography, culture and civic life for youth aged about 10 to 17. Your child's class will use it a few sessions a week for 4 to 6 weeks. There is also a small study on how well it works.
pages.consentForm.formIntro.source: {organisation} is trying Thinkerwell, a free online course about history, geography, culture and civic life for youth aged about 10 to 17. Your child's class will use it a few sessions a week for 4 to 6 weeks. There is also a small study of how well it works.

pages.consentForm.choiceBody.note: Back-translation check: Changed 'tetap diambil kira' (merely 'taken into account') to 'keputusannya itu dihormati' so that the child's no is final, matching learnerWins. Please check this reads naturally and firmly. The same change was made in infoSheet.choiceBody.
pages.consentForm.choiceBody.back: If you answer no to any of the questions below, this will not affect anything else your child does at {organisation}. If you answer no to this study, your child can still use Thinkerwell in class; it's just that their answers are not used. You can change your mind at any time, even after the pilot programme: tell {organisation}, and your child's answers will be deleted. Your child can also say no, and their decision to say no is still taken into account.
pages.consentForm.choiceBody.source: Saying no to either question below won't affect anything else your child does at {organisation}. If you say no to the study, your child can still use Thinkerwell in class; their answers just aren't used. You can change your mind at any time, even after the pilot: tell {organisation}, and your child's answers are deleted. Your child can say no too, and their no counts.

pages.infoSheet.choiceBody.back: This is your choice, and you answer on the consent form. If you say no to this study, your child still comes to class and can still use Thinkerwell. It's just that their answers are not used in the study. You can change your mind at any time, even after the pilot programme. Tell the teacher, and your child's answers will be deleted. Your child can also say no, and their decision to say no is still taken into account.

pages.about.missionBody.back: Thinkerwell began from a love of social studies and one question: how can more youth get the chance to explore the world they live in? We built a free digital platform so that digital learning tools and social studies education are easily accessible to youth who face educational barriers. Our goal is to help students ask questions, develop their critical thinking skills, explore various perspectives and share their own ideas.
pages.about.missionBody.source: Thinkerwell began with a love of social studies and a question: how can more youth have the chance to explore the world they live in? We built a free digital platform to make digital learning tools and social studies education accessible to youth facing barriers to education. Our goal is to help learners ask questions, grow their critical thinking skills, explore diverse perspectives, and share their own ideas.

siteVideo.explore.p1.back: Every student deserves the chance to explore the world they live in. But across Southeast Asia, many youth face educational barriers. In Myanmar, about 3.8 million people have been forced to leave their homes but are still inside their own country. In Malaysia, refugee children cannot attend government schools. And in East Asia and the Pacific, one in three school-age children does not have internet at home.
siteVideo.explore.p1.source: Every learner deserves the chance to explore the world they live in. But across Southeast Asia, many youth face barriers to education. In Myanmar, about 3.8 million people are displaced inside their own country. In Malaysia, refugee children can't attend government schools. And in East Asia and the Pacific, one in three school-age children had no internet at home.

siteVideo.explore.p2.back: When schools are overburdened, lessons often focus only on the basics: reading, maths and skills for work. All of that is important. But only a little room is left for the skills that open up the world: thinking critically, communicating with evidence and seeing from other people's perspectives.
siteVideo.explore.p2.source: Where schools are stretched, lessons often stick to the basics: reading, maths, and skills for a job. Those matter. But there's little room left for the skills that open up the world: thinking critically, communicating with evidence, and taking other perspectives.

siteVideo.explore.p3.back: Research supports this. In one Stanford study, students who learned history by questioning real sources showed greater progress in historical thinking, reading and knowledge than students in ordinary classes.
siteVideo.explore.p3.source: Research backs this up. In a Stanford study, students who learned history by questioning real sources grew more in historical thinking, reading, and knowledge than students in regular classes.

siteVideo.explore.p4.back: That is why we built Thinkerwell: free lessons in social studies and more, for youth who face educational barriers. Our first course, Exploring Our World, has 24 lessons on history, geography, culture and civic life, and each lesson has five steps: read, write, speak, watch and reflect. Every reading has a simpler version and can be read aloud, and the lessons can be used offline, in English and Bahasa Indonesia.

digitalWorld.switch.saveFailed.back: This device could not save that setting. It only takes effect until you close this page.
digitalWorld.switch.saveFailed.source: This device couldn't save that. It applies until you close this page.

digitalWorld.tool.badge.note: Translator: "Pretend tool" is translated as "Alat rekaan", to match "Contoh rekaan" in the key terms. "Alat olok-olok" sounds more playful. Check whether young readers understand it as pretend or made-up, or whether "Alat olok-olok" is clearer. The choice also applies to tool.toolSays and tool.paperAnswers.

digitalWorld.tool.paperAnswers.note: Translator: "Gesaan" is the usual Malaysian word for an AI prompt, but young readers may not know it. "arahan" or "soalan" are simpler options. Check that it sounds natural to children, or add the English term in brackets.

digitalWorld.trainModel.newExamples.back: There are {count} new examples. Give each one a label, and it will move to that group.

digitalWorld.trainModel.noNewExamples.back: No new examples this time. Test the model with leaves from a new tree.
digitalWorld.trainModel.noNewExamples.source: No new examples this time. Test the model on leaves from a new plant.

digitalWorld.trainModel.toSortTitle.note: Translator: "Isih" means sort. Check that learners know it. "Untuk diasingkan" is another option. Back-translation check: The translator's flag still stands. digitalWorld.trainModel.trainHelpEmpty.back: Give a label to at least one leaf to train the model.
